content.value_statement: Building Azure OpenAI features in .NET requires correct clients, authentication, and service-specific SDK patterns. This skill provides focused C# guidance for chat, embeddings, media, RAG, tools, and production practices.
actual_capabilities: Explains Azure OpenAI client setup with API keys or Microsoft Entra ID.
Provides patterns for synchronous, asynchronous, streaming, and multi-turn chat.
Covers structured outputs, reasoning options, token usage, and request configuration.
Shows embeddings and Azure AI Search integration with citations.
Documents image generation, transcription, speech generation, and audio clients.
Covers function calling, tool argument validation, rate limits, and SDK error handling.
limitations: The skill provides reference guidance and does not execute, compile, test, or deploy applications.
Users must supply their own Azure resources, deployments, credentials, and service permissions.
Model features and SDK APIs can vary by region, deployment, package version, and service configuration.
Examples require environment-specific validation before production use.

use_cases.title: Create a .NET AI prototype
use_cases.description: Set up authentication and add basic or streaming chat to a new C# application.

use_cases.title: Add retrieval to enterprise data
use_cases.description: Connect Azure OpenAI with Azure AI Search and return grounded answers with citations.

use_cases.title: Standardize production SDK patterns
use_cases.description: Review client reuse, identity, retries, token monitoring, structured outputs, and tool validation.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a first client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure Azure.AI.OpenAI in a .NET console application using Microsoft Entra ID. Include required packages and environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Build streaming chat
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an asynchronous, streaming chat workflow for [application type] using deployment [deployment name]. Explain client reuse, cancellation, token tracking, and 429 handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design structured output
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a structured-output workflow that returns [business object] for input [sample input]. Define validation requirements and explain how to parse the response safely.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a grounded assistant
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET RAG workflow using Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search for [data source]. Include authentication, citations, tool-call validation, retries, and observability.

output_examples.input: Recommend an authentication approach for a production Azure OpenAI service.
output_examples.output: Use Microsoft Entra ID with DefaultAzureCredential. Assign only required roles, reuse the client, and avoid storing API keys in application settings.

output_examples.input: Outline a reliable streaming chat implementation for a customer support application.
output: Create one reusable chat client for the configured deployment.
Stream updates asynchronously and honor cancellation requests.
Track token usage and retry rate-limited requests with backoff.
Validate content and tool arguments before downstream actions.

output_examples.input: Explain how to ground answers with Azure AI Search.
output_examples.output: Configure an Azure Search data source, authenticate securely, request chat completion, and expose returned citations with the answer.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID and least-privilege roles for production authentication.
Reuse client instances, set timeouts, and handle rate limits with controlled retries.
Validate structured responses and tool arguments before using them in application actions.
anti_patterns: Do not place production API keys in prompts, source files, logs, or generated examples.
Do not execute model-provided tool arguments without schema validation and authorization checks.
Do not assume every model, region, or deployment supports the same SDK features.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure OpenAI requests?
faq.answer: No. It provides .NET implementation guidance and examples, but it does not execute requests or deploy resources.

faq.question: Which authentication methods are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Azure API key authentication and Microsoft Entra ID through DefaultAzureCredential.

faq.question: Which package version does the source reference?
faq.answer: The source references Azure.AI.OpenAI 2.1.0. Verify the latest supported version before implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with streaming and multi-turn chat?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents asynchronous streaming, message history, request options, and token usage.

faq.question: Does it cover retrieval-augmented generation?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows Azure AI Search integration, data-source authentication, message context, and citations.

faq.question: What must I provide?
faq.answer: Provide an Azure endpoint, deployment names, suitable credentials, permissions, and application requirements.
